\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{بكالوريوس} (bakālūriyūs)}{بكالوريوس (bakālūriyūs)}]{\ar{بكالوريوس} (bakālūriyūs) — a bachelor's degree}

\label{lesson:AR-C397-bakaluriyus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a thesis, then the Arabic for a curriculum.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{بكالوريوس}}
\textbf{\ar{بكالوريوس}} — \emph{bakālūriyūs} — \textquotedblleft{}a bachelor's degree\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{حصل} \ar{أخي} \ar{على} \ar{البكالوريوس} \ar{في} \ar{التجارة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḥaṣala akhī ʿalā al-bakālūriyūs fī at-tijāra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother got a bachelor's degree in commerce.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{بكالوريوس}} (\emph{bakālūriyūs}) is a modern loan, usually traced to medieval Latin \emph{baccalaureus}, the holder of a first degree. Arabic keeps the Latin ending.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bakālūriyūs}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bakālūriyūs}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥaṣala akhī ʿalā al-bakālūriyūs fī at-tijāra.} — My brother got a bachelor's degree in commerce.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a thesis, then the Arabic for a curriculum, then say \emph{bakālūriyūs} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{بكالوريوس} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A bachelor's degree\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ماجستير} (mājistīr)}{ماجستير (mājistīr)}]{\ar{ماجستير} (mājistīr) — a master's degree}

\label{lesson:AR-C397-majistir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a curriculum, then the Arabic for a bachelor's degree.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ماجستير}}
\textbf{\ar{ماجستير}} — \emph{mājistīr} — \textquotedblleft{}a master's degree\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تدرس} \ar{أختي} \ar{الماجستير} \ar{في} \ar{الأدب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tadrusu ukhtī al-mājistīr fī al-adab.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister is studying for a master's degree in literature.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ماجستير}} (\emph{mājistīr}) is a modern loan, usually traced to Latin \emph{magister}, \textquotedblleft{}a master, a teacher\textquotedblright{}, through European names for the degree.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a curriculum, then the Arabic for a bachelor's degree, then say \emph{mājistīr} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{دكتوراه} (duktūrāh)}{دكتوراه (duktūrāh)}]{\ar{دكتوراه} (duktūrāh) — a doctorate}

\label{lesson:AR-C397-duktura}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a bachelor's degree, then the Arabic for a master's degree.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{دكتوراه}}
\textbf{\ar{دكتوراه}} — \emph{duktūrāh} — \textquotedblleft{}a doctorate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كتب} \ar{أبي} \ar{أطروحة} \ar{الدكتوراه} \ar{في} \ar{عامين}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kataba abī uṭrūḥat ad-duktūrāh fī ʿāmayn.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father wrote his doctoral thesis in two years.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{دكتوراه}} (\emph{duktūrāh}) is a modern loan, usually traced to Latin \emph{doctor}, \textquotedblleft{}a teacher\textquotedblright{}, through European languages. Its final h is written with \ar{ه}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a bachelor's degree, then the Arabic for a master's degree, then say \emph{duktūrāh} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مقرر} (muqarrar)}{مقرر (muqarrar)}]{\ar{مقرر} (muqarrar) — a syllabus}

\label{lesson:AR-C397-muqarrar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a master's degree, then the Arabic for a doctorate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مقرر}}
\textbf{\ar{مقرر}} — \emph{muqarrar} — \textquotedblleft{}a syllabus\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{هذا} \ar{الكتاب} \ar{جزء} \ar{من} \ar{المقرر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hādhā al-kitāb juzʾ min al-muqarrar.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This book is part of the syllabus.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مقرر}} (\emph{muqarrar}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-r-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to settle, to be still\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Muqarrar} is the Form II passive participle, what has been fixed: a set syllabus. \ar{قرار}, a decision, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muqarrar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muqarrar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hādhā al-kitāb juzʾ min al-muqarrar.} — This book is part of the syllabus.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a master's degree, then the Arabic for a doctorate, then say \emph{muqarrar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مقرر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A syllabus\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تدريب} (tadrīb)}{تدريب (tadrīb)}]{\ar{تدريب} (tadrīb) — training}

\label{lesson:AR-C397-tadrib}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a doctorate, then the Arabic for a syllabus.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تدريب}}
\textbf{\ar{تدريب}} — \emph{tadrīb} — \textquotedblleft{}training\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يحتاج} \ar{الموظفون} \ar{الجدد} \ar{إلى} \ar{تدريب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yaḥtāju al-muwaẓẓafūn al-judud ilā tadrīb.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
New employees need training.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تدريب}} (\emph{tadrīb}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-r-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to be used to, practised\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Tadrīb} is the Form II verbal noun, making someone practised: training. \ar{مدرب}, a coach, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tadrīb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yaḥtāju al-muwaẓẓafūn al-judud ilā tadrīb.} — New employees need training.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a doctorate, then the Arabic for a syllabus, then say \emph{tadrīb} again
\end{itemize}

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 390–397 — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R397-review-390-397}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for a faculty and a specialization.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a faculty, a specialization, a dean, a scholarship, to enrol
  \item a researcher, a study, a laboratory, an institute, a questionnaire
  \item a lecturer, a professor, to supervise, a supervisor, to study for
  \item a test, admission, an average, to excel, to evaluate
  \item to master, to acquire, to go deeper, to summarize, a summary
  \item a reference, to cite, to quote, to read up on, to reflect
  \item a term, a definition, an index, a thesis, a curriculum
  \item a bachelor's degree, a master's degree, a doctorate, a syllabus, training
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A faculty? (\textbf{\ar{كلية}}, \emph{kulliyya}.) A specialization? (\textbf{\ar{تخصص}}, \emph{takhaṣṣuṣ}.) A dean? (\textbf{\ar{عميد}}, \emph{ʿamīd}.) A scholarship? (\textbf{\ar{منحة}}, \emph{minḥa}.) To enrol? (\textbf{\ar{التحق}}, \emph{iltaḥaqa}.) A researcher? (\textbf{\ar{باحث}}, \emph{bāḥith}.) A study? (\textbf{\ar{دراسة}}, \emph{dirāsa}.) A laboratory? (\textbf{\ar{مختبر}}, \emph{mukhtabar}.) An institute? (\textbf{\ar{معهد}}, \emph{maʿhad}.) A questionnaire? (\textbf{\ar{استبيان}}, \emph{istibyān}.) A lecturer? (\textbf{\ar{محاضر}}, \emph{muḥāḍir}.) A professor? (\textbf{\ar{أستاذ}}, \emph{ustādh}.) To supervise? (\textbf{\ar{أشرف}}, \emph{ashrafa}.) A supervisor? (\textbf{\ar{مشرف}}, \emph{mushrif}.) To study for? (\textbf{\ar{ذاكر}}, \emph{dhākara}.) A test? (\textbf{\ar{اختبار}}, \emph{ikhtibār}.) Admission? (\textbf{\ar{قبول}}, \emph{qabūl}.) An average? (\textbf{\ar{معدل}}, \emph{muʿaddal}.) To excel? (\textbf{\ar{تفوق}}, \emph{tafawwaqa}.) To evaluate? (\textbf{\ar{قيم}}, \emph{qayyama}.) To master? (\textbf{\ar{أتقن}}, \emph{atqana}.) To acquire? (\textbf{\ar{اكتسب}}, \emph{iktasaba}.) To go deeper? (\textbf{\ar{تعمق}}, \emph{taʿammaqa}.) To summarize? (\textbf{\ar{لخص}}, \emph{lakhkhaṣa}.) A summary? (\textbf{\ar{ملخص}}, \emph{mulakhkhaṣ}.) A reference? (\textbf{\ar{مرجع}}, \emph{marjiʿ}.) To cite? (\textbf{\ar{استشهد}}, \emph{istashhada}.) To quote? (\textbf{\ar{اقتبس}}, \emph{iqtabasa}.) To read up on? (\textbf{\ar{طالع}}, \emph{ṭālaʿa}.) To reflect? (\textbf{\ar{تأمل}}, \emph{taʾammala}.) A term? (\textbf{\ar{مصطلح}}, \emph{muṣṭalaḥ}.) A definition? (\textbf{\ar{تعريف}}, \emph{taʿrīf}.) An index? (\textbf{\ar{فهرس}}, \emph{fihris}.) A thesis? (\textbf{\ar{أطروحة}}, \emph{uṭrūḥa}.) A curriculum? (\textbf{\ar{منهج}}, \emph{manhaj}.) A bachelor's degree? (\textbf{\ar{بكالوريوس}}, \emph{bakālūriyūs}.) A master's degree? (\textbf{\ar{ماجستير}}, \emph{mājistīr}.) A doctorate? (\textbf{\ar{دكتوراه}}, \emph{duktūrāh}.) A syllabus? (\textbf{\ar{مقرر}}, \emph{muqarrar}.) Training? (\textbf{\ar{تدريب}}, \emph{tadrīb}.)
